3/16.01.2024:

By filing this petition, the petitioner has prayed for direction to the respondents to pay compensation in respect of the land of Jamabandi No. 47/28 of Mouza- Tiurngar, Thana No.
854, 860 under Circle Mohanpur, District- Deoghar, area-12.42 acres, which has been acquired and is recorded in the name of the predecessor of the petitioner.

The petitioner further claims that proper award be prepared in their names in respect of the land which has been acquired for construction of National Highway 114A.
2.
Counsel for the petitioner submits that through the land was acquired, yet no award has been prepared in the name of these petitioners, who are the land loosers and descendants of khatiyani raiyats.
He submits that the award should have been prepared in the name of these petitioners.
It is his contention that since the award has not been prepared in the name of the petitioners, the amount will be paid to some other persons who are not entitled to receive the amount.
3. Counsel for the State opposes the prayer and submits that there is an alternative remedy available under the National Highway Act, 1956.

By referring to Section 3(H) of the Act specially subsection Mahendra Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190067215/
1 (3) and (4), the counsel for the State argues that the petitioners should approach the Competent Authority.

sentences.text: 4. After hearing the counsel for the parties, I find that the petitioners are claiming compensation after preparation of the award in the name of the petitioners.

Section 3H of National Highway Act reads as follows;
"3H. Deposit and payment of amount.--(1) The amount determined under section 3G shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner asmay be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government, with the competent authority before taking possession of the land.

(2) As soon as may be after the amount has been deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall on behalf of the Central Government pay the amount to the person or persons entitled thereto.

(3) Where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

(4) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

(5) Where the amount determined under section 3G by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the arbitrator may award interest at nine per cent, per annum on such excess amount from the date of taking possession under section 3D till the date of the actual deposit thereof.

(6) Where the amount determined by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the excess amount together with interest, if any, awarded under sub-section (5) shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner as may be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government,
with the competent authority and the provisions of subsections (2) to (4) shall apply to such deposit.
5. As per the aforesaid provisions, it is only the Competent Authority who can decide apportionment of the amount and determine as to who is the persons to receive the same.

Further, as per Sub-Section(4) of Section 3(H) of the Act, if there is any dispute, the competent authority is given a power to refer the dispute before a civil court having original jurisdiction for decision.

6. Thus, I am of opinion that the petitioner should approach the Competent Authority who should take appropriate decision and pass appropriate order as per Sub-Sections (3)/(4) of Section 3(H) of the National Highways Act.
7. With the aforesaid observation and direction, this petition stands disposed of.
